title: spec review: S2b v4: capacity treats claude:<tier> rows as Claude capacity (account cooling folded into row cooling, shared worker cap); README plug-and-play
spec:
Goal T-1334 (S1 T-1352 merged). Replaces T-1363 after spec review T-1364 (no high findings; mediums fixed below). Claude executor rows have id "claude:<tier>" (S2a T-1360); running claude-row tasks carry executor "claude:<tier>", counted by daemon.running_claude_workers (daemon.py:470), which also counts Claude review/scout workers on purpose: all share max_parallel_claude_workers. Fallback keeps today's meaning: every enabled execute row cooling, never merely saturated (daemon.py:481 docstring). executor.start -> pool.pick stays authoritative at dispatch.

Rule R: a claude row is cooling when its own cooldown is active, OR there are zero Claude accounts, OR every Claude account is cooling. Codex rows as today.
Shared Claude capacity C: outside fallback mode C = max_parallel_claude_workers - running_claude_workers (no inflight subtraction: inflight_claude_dispatches counts Codex dispatches too); in fallback mode unchanged from today (also minus inflight_claude_dispatches).
1. capacity.snapshot (capacity.py:9): rows carry "provider" (readers use row.get("provider", "codex")); claude row cooling_s = row cooldown if active; else 3600 when there are zero accounts; else the smallest account cooldown when every account cools; else 0. snapshot["claude_workers_free"] keeps its current value for the legacy fallback; add snapshot["claude_rows_free"] = C computed with the outside-fallback formula (the caller passes running_claude as today).
2. capacity.admit (:101): free["claude_rows"] = snapshot.get("claude_rows_free", 0); eff(id) = min(free[id], free["claude_rows"]) for claude rows else free[id]; use eff in the `available` filter (:127), choice_key (:132) and the imminent blocker (:141, `eff(id) == 1`). Choosing a claude row decrements both.
3. capacity._reason: claude row otherwise eligible with free["claude_rows"] == 0 -> "account_capacity".
4. orchestrator/daemon.py: _codex_available (:454) applies R through the pool. free_slots (:481): outside fallback, codex rows as today plus min(sum over claude rows that are enabled, execute, not cooling under R, within band-independent day budget (daily_budget_tasks 0 or day_tasks < budget) of max_parallel - running, C). capacity_reason (:772): apply R for "every enabled row cooling", and return "account_capacity" when the only non-cooling rows are claude rows and C == 0.
5. Known follow-up (not this task): a routed claude dispatch that finds no headroom is held "no account with headroom" and the daemon only retries budget holds; concurrency.py / speculation.py read per-row free. Recorded in plan.md.
6. README.md "Executors and routing" (README.md:278): Claude rows (id "claude:<tier>", tier alias in [models], model optional and must match, roles, band, max_parallel, daily_budget_tasks), headroom from [[claude_accounts]] and [limits].max_parallel_claude_workers (shared with Claude reviews and scouts), reviewer never runs the executing model, plug-and-play: [models] alias + claude:<alias> row for a new Claude model; a codex row for a new Codex model; enabled=false on every codex row to run without Codex.
Tests (unittest.TestCase methods, one per acceptance id). No pool.toml edit, no new dependencies. Additive; git revert restores the old behaviour.

risks.issue: Rule R is implemented twice: from snapshot data in capacity.snapshot, and 'through the pool' in daemon._codex_available and capacity_reason. The two can drift, and the daemon and admit would then disagree on cooling. It is also unclear whether the daemon version calls pool.pick(), which rolls state. pool.eligible_executors already does this at pool.py:563-566. The snapshot must stay read-only.

The snapshot 'fallback' flag is all(enabled execute rows cooling_s > 0), and claude rows can now cool through account state. With Codex cooling and every Claude account cooling, fallback turns on and eligible_executors_from_snapshot returns ['claude']. daemon._fallback_mode does the same. That routes to a Claude tier that has no headroom, so it fails at pool.pick instead of holding with reason 'cooldown'. This contradicts the claim that fallback keeps today's meaning. The spec says nothing about fallback when the Claude accounts themselves are cooling.

The claude_rows_free formula uses max - running_claude_workers with no inflight subtraction. Claude-row dispatches that were sent but not yet claimed (queued, dispatched_at set, not gated) are counted nowhere. Several dispatches in one tick or across consecutive ticks can oversubscribe the cap shared with Claude reviews and scouts. Only the late pool.pick guards against it, and that guard turns into a 'no account with headroom' hold. Only Codex-row inflight should be excluded. Inflight dispatches whose executor or assigned id starts with 'claude:' should be included.

The free_slots day-budget check reads ex.day_tasks directly. Executor.day_tasks is only reset by roll_day(), so a row that hit its budget yesterday stays 'over budget' until something else rolls it. snapshot() handles this with effective_day_tasks, but the daemon path in the spec does not.

free_slots sums per-row (max_parallel - running) for claude rows and ignores complexity bands, so it overstates slots. That only matters if the scheduler is off or in shadow mode. In those modes admit() never runs, so the shared cap C is enforced only by min(sum, C), and the per-row band mismatch is left to executor.start. Acknowledged in item 5, but the tick-level slot count will churn holds.

A fabricated cooling_s of 3600 for zero accounts is an arbitrary constant that shows up in status and scorecard output as a fake cooldown. Snapshot cooling_s for a claude row does not include utilization or window-cap exhaustion, which pool.pick also checks. So 'not cooling' still does not mean 'has headroom'.

free['claude_rows'] shares a dict with executor ids. A row named 'claude_rows' would collide, and the claude row test relies on row.get('provider'). The pseudo-id 'claude' in fallback mode has no provider row, so eff() must treat it as unshared.

There are no acceptance tests for these paths. The first is day-budget rollover in free_slots. The second is the fallback path when both Codex and all Claude accounts are cooling. The third is capacity_reason returning 'account_capacity' versus 'cooldown' for a claude-only pool. The README change has no test, and tests/test_README.py is missing. Line numbers in the spec are off by 1-3 (_codex_available is at 455 and free_slots at 484), so the executor should locate by symbol.

suggested_spec_changes: Put rule R in one helper, for example capacity.claude_row_cooling_s(pool, now), that only reads state (no pool.pick, no roll). Have snapshot(), _codex_available and capacity_reason all call it.

State what fallback means when claude rows cool because of account state. Recommended: fallback_mode requires at least one Codex-provider row to exist and cool, and it is off when Claude accounts are all cooling. Reason 'cooldown' is returned, not 'account_capacity'. Add a test for this.

Include dispatched-but-unclaimed execute tasks whose executor id starts with 'claude:' in the claude_rows_free subtraction, or explicitly justify why oversubscription is acceptable. Decrement free['claude_rows'] within a tick as specified.
In daemon.free_slots, compute the effective day_tasks the same way snapshot does (roll_day or a date comparison) instead of reading ex.day_tasks raw. Add a test for a stale day.
Replace the 3600 magic value with a named constant, or use a distinct flag such as 'no_accounts': True alongside cooling_s.

Name the key as 'claude_rows_free' only and reserve it against executor-id collisions. Say how eff() identifies claude rows (row.get('provider') == 'claude') and that the fallback pseudo-id 'claude' is unaffected.
Add a rollback note: the change is additive and git revert of the task commit restores the old behaviour. The spec already says this, so keep it in the commit message and decisions.md.
